Welcome to Energy Ratings of Australia!

Your guide to choosing energy-efficient appliances for a sustainable Australian home.

Did you know?

The Australian Energy Rating Label helps you compare the energy efficiency and running costs of appliances before you buy.

Television Energy Consumption

Modern LED and OLED TVs vary significantly in power usage.

TV Type Star Rating Annual Consumption of Television (kwh/yr)
OLED ★★★★★ 325.062 kWh
LCD ★★★★★★ 363.90 kWh

About Us

We created this site to help Aussie households understand the Energy Rating Label. While most people look at screen size, we look at the 10-year running cost so you don't get shock when the power bill arrives.

The Issue

Televisions are a major energy consumer in Australian homes.

Demonstration Issue: Data Research

Here's a sample of the data that has been researched on for Television Energy Consumption in Australia

Screen Type Average Power (W) Efficiency Status
LCD (LED) 73.40 Best for Usage
OLED 86.94 Medium Usage
LCD 96.45 High Energy Usage

Based on the data from data.gov.au and processed using KNIME, it is shown that LCD (LED) models have a higher average power consumption compared to OLED and LCD screen.

Why? This is likely due to Australia having bigger LCD screen size models in the market compared to OLED models.

Ideas to Overcome Energy Consumption in Australian Homes

  • Opt for television with Energy Star labels, which are design to consume less power and reduce energy usage.
  • Optimise TV settings such as reducing screen brightness and enabling power saving mode.
  • Turn off when not in use instead of leaving it on standby mode.

Our Goals

  • Reducing television usage by minimising electricity usage and carbon footprint.

Charts

Average power consumptions by screen technology across 347 TV models available in Australia:

Recommendation

After comparing screen technology by their power consumptions, LCD (LED) TVs consumed the least power at 73.40W, compared to LCD screen at 96.45W. For consumers that like to purchase the least power consumption television, LCD (LED) is the most efficient choice.

The Issue

With so many TV brands in Australia, consumers don't know which brand offers the most variety and choice of models.

Demonstration Issue: Data Research

Table below is data showing a few brands and their model.

Brands Model Number
Samsung Electronics 731
LG 683
Kogan 416
Hisense 323

Based on the data on data.gov.au and the processing of KNIME, the models with the most variety is Samsung Electronics and LG.

Why? Samsung Electronics and LG have a wider range of models available in the Australian market, offering consumers more options in terms of size, features, and price points.

Ideas to Overcome

  • Search for brands that have variety of models as some consumers have budgets.
  • Compare models within the same brand to get better deals.
  • Check for energy ratings across models for the lest power consumption.

Our Goals

  • Help identify what brands offers the most varieties in Australia so that they are able to make better purchasing decisions.

Charts

The brands with the highest number of models in Australia.

Recommendations

After comparison of which TV brand has the highest models, Samsung Electronics has the highest number of models, followed by LG with the second highest models, giving consumers a wider range of options to choose from.
